title: Longest Nice Substring
summary: A string is considered nice if it includes every letter in both uppercase and lowercase.
statement: A string is considered nice if it includes every letter in both uppercase and lowercase. Given a string, find the longest nice substring. If multiple exist, choose the earliest one. Return an empty string if no nice substring is found.
constraints: A substring is nice when every letter it contains appears in both lowercase and uppercase.
Return the longest nice substring; when lengths tie, return the earliest one.
hints: If a character lacks its opposite case in the current string, no nice substring can cross that character.
Split at the first offending character and solve both sides recursively.
Return the longer result, choosing the left result on equal lengths; if no character offends, return the whole string.
Every feasible substring lies wholly on one side of each offending character, so divide-and-conquer loses no candidate.
editorial: Every feasible substring lies wholly on one side of each offending character, so divide-and-conquer loses no candidate.
